name: English I
description: This course consists of a study of various texts with a focus on the characteristics of literary genres including poetry, drama, short and long fiction, and nonfiction. Students will practice research, presentation skills and composition, with a focus on the interrelationship of these areas.

name: Honors English I
description: This course consists of a study of various texts with a focus on the characteristics of literary genres including poetry, drama, short and long fiction, and nonfiction. Students will practice research, presentation skills and composition, with a focus on the interrelationship of these areas.

name: English II
description: Activities in English II continue to be focused on the study of language, literature, and writing. Students will examine various archetypes in classical and contemporary works of literature. The essential questions that guide the course are: • What stories have we told and do we continue to tell? Why? • Whose stories are missing and how does that impact society as a whole?
prereqText: Prerequisite: 9th Grade English

Why? • Whose stories are missing and how does that impact society as a whole?

name: English III
description: The Classic and Contemporary Course puts classical texts in conversation with modern texts. With a focus on American literature, the class aims to bridge themes that resonate throughout time and history while opening up conversation for students to relate to texts in an authentic and personal way.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 10th Grade English

name: American Studies
description: This course takes the place of 11th grade US History II and English III. Students will fulfill their graduation requirements and credit for both 11th grade American History and 11th grade English. American Studies provides an interdisciplinary examination of the historical, political, social, cultural, and literary heritage of the United States from the industrial era to contemporary times. Counts toward both English and Social Studies. The 5 + 5 credit split is unverified.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 10th Grade English & History*

Students will fulfill their graduation requirements and credit for both 11th grade American History and 11th grade English. American Studies provides an interdisciplinary examination of the historical, political, social, cultural, and literary heritage of the United States from the industrial era to contemporary times. Counts toward both English and Social Studies. The 5 + 5 credit split is unverified.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 10th Grade English & History*

name: English IV
description: World Literature/Honors World Literature is a senior-level English course designed to further students' understanding, appreciation, and comprehension of classic and contemporary literature from a variety of authors from around the world. Additionally, students will practice their writing skills in argumentative, narrative, and expository modes.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 11th Grade English

Additionally, students will practice their writing skills in argumentative, narrative, and expository modes.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 11th Grade English

name: AP Capstone: Seminar
description: This is the first in a required two-course sequence (AP Capstone) that focuses on research skills and argumentation. This interdisciplinary course will prepare students for success in future courses across all content areas and in college.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 9th Grade English

name: AP Capstone: Research
description: From the College Board website: “Build on what you learned in AP Seminar to deeply explore an academic topic, problem, or issue of individual interest. Through this exploration, you will design, plan, and conduct a year-long research-based investigation to address a research question.” This course may be taught by a teacher in any content area and students may undertake research projects in any content area. Elective. Does not count for English credit.
prereqText: Prerequisite: AP Seminar

name: Reading Science Fiction Literature
description: This course is a junior English course that encourages students to explore humanity's relationships with technology and the natural world. During various units, students will read classic and contemporary texts about artificial intelligence, genetic engineering, space exploration, and the environment. Additionally, students will practice their writing skills in argumentative, narrative, and expository modes.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 10th Grade English

Additionally, students will practice their writing skills in argumentative, narrative, and expository modes.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 10th Grade English

name: Language, Myth, and Culture
description: This course will focus on the types of writing and reading skills needed to excel in college. Students will practice analytical, persuasive, and narrative forms of writing through a writing workshop format.

name: Honors Language, Myth, and Culture
description: This course will focus on the types of writing and reading skills needed to excel in college. Students will practice analytical, persuasive, and narrative forms of writing through a writing workshop format.
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Seton Hall University.

name: Sports and Literature
description: This multi-media college preparatory course, with a focus on literature, will introduce the history and importance of sports in our society. The students will be introduced to important figures, trends, and developments in sports as well as utilize print and visual media about sports.

name: Philosophy and Literature
description: Great literature asks many questions of its readers: What should we do? Why are we here? How should we live? As such, the Philosophy and Literature course asks students to consider the questions that have intrigued, challenged, and bewildered thinkers and writers for millennia.

name: Honors Philosophy and Literature
description: Great literature asks many questions of its readers: What should we do? Why are we here? How should we live? As such, the Philosophy and Literature course asks students to consider the questions that have intrigued, challenged, and bewildered thinkers and writers for millennia.

name: Honors Drama and Shakespeare
description: This is a senior-level English course designed to further students' understanding, appreciation, and comprehension of the drama genre. Students will delve into the works of Shakespeare and his contemporaries, texts written by ancient playwrights, and well-known plays from the modern era.

name: Literature of the Holocaust
description: This course will expose students to the events of the Holocaust through a wide variety of fiction, drama and poetry written during and after the Holocaust by authors, survivors and witnesses.

name: Honors Literature of the Holocaust
description: This course will expose students to the events of the Holocaust through a wide variety of fiction, drama and poetry written during and after the Holocaust by authors, survivors and witnesses.
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Kean University.

name: AP Language and Composition
description: This Advanced Placement course may be accepted for college credit at a number of participating colleges and universities upon the student’s successful completion of the College Board’s Advanced Placement Examination in English Language and Composition. Students are highly encouraged to take the Advanced Placement Examination in May.

name: AP Literature and Composition
description: This Advanced Placement course may be accepted for college credit at a number of participating colleges and universities upon the student’s successful completion of the College Board’s Advanced Placement Examination in English Literature and Composition. Students are highly encouraged to take the Advanced Placement Examination in May.

name: 21st Century Journalism & Media
description: 21st Century Journalism & Media is a full year elective publication course. The emphasis in this course is on desktop publishing (newspapers, magazines, photography, yearbooks, fliers, brochures, ads, etc.). This is a product-based, hands-on class.

name: Honors Advanced 21st Century Journalism & Media
description: Honors Advanced 21st Century Journalism & Media is an opportunity for students to immerse themselves in an intensive, largely self-directed experience during which they will produce a variety of multimedia content. This class will provide an avenue toward web, broadcast, and print product, and digital tools and alternative storytelling techniques will be emphasized.
prereqText: Prerequisite for the class is 21st Century Journalism & Media

name: Honors Advanced 21st Century Journalism & Media II
description: Honors Advanced 21st Century Journalism & Media II offers the student, who has successfully completed Honors Advanced 21st Century Journalism & Media, an opportunity to further develop their writing, reporting, layout, speaking, editing, computer, management, business, and photography skills.
prereqText: Prerequisite for the class is Honors Advanced 21st Century Journalism & Media

name: Film and Literature: Understanding Movies from Script to Screen
description: This course will provide the opportunity for students to approach film with an understanding of and an appreciation for the techniques employed in the evolution of film from concept to screen.

name: Creative Writing
description: Creative Writing is a full-year, five-credit course designed for students who wish to explore a variety of genres. Readings in multiple genres, lessons in a variety of writing techniques, intense writing practice and self-evaluation are the basis of this course. The class is run in a workshop model, through ongoing writing, sharing, and revising work.

name: Theater Arts
description: Theater Arts I is a full year, five credit elective course for freshmen, sophomores, juniors, or seniors. The course consists of a study of theater as an art form, with special emphasis placed on analysis and practice of the physical and vocal aspects of acting. Acting styles from different periods of theater are explored, and a wide variety of plays and characters are studied.

name: Public Speaking
description: Public speaking is not just about formal presentations. This course will address all the important aspects of public speaking, including but not limited to, audience, content and delivery. Students will be exposed to a variety of effective speeches from literature, history, film and current events.

name: World History
description: The purpose of this course is to introduce the major historic events, concepts, and ideas in world history. The chronological emphasis will begin in the Middle Ages and draw from those themes and concepts students learned about the ancient, classical, and medieval worlds. Additionally, European civilization will be analyzed and students will learn how it influenced the rest of the world. 23

name: Honors World History
description: The purpose of this course is to introduce the major historic events, concepts, and ideas in world history. The chronological emphasis will begin in the Middle Ages and draw from those themes and concepts students learned about the ancient, classical, and medieval worlds. Additionally, European civilization will be analyzed and students will learn how it influenced the rest of the world. 23 Honors placement is by recommendation of teacher and supervisor.

name: U.S. History I
description: This course provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the development of the American nation through analysis of the following periods of major change in America’s history: the Foundation and Expansionary Periods, Nationalism and Sectionalism, Industrial Development and Economics.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 9th Grade World History

name: Honors U.S. History I
description: This course provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the development of the American nation through analysis of the following periods of major change in America’s history: the Foundation and Expansionary Periods, Nationalism and Sectionalism, Industrial Development and Economics. Honors placement is by recommendation of teacher and supervisor.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 9th Grade World History

name: U.S. History II
description: This course provides students with an understanding of the knowledge and attitudes of the American people since the later part of the 19th century. Imperialism, Globalization, and American Expansionism are highlighted through the study of domestic and global social, political, and economic issues.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 10th Grade U. S. History I

name: Honors U.S. History II
description: This course provides students with an understanding of the knowledge and attitudes of the American people since the later part of the 19th century. Imperialism, Globalization, and American Expansionism are highlighted through the study of domestic and global social, political, and economic issues. Honors placement is by recommendation of teacher and supervisor.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 10th Grade U. S. History I

name: AP U.S. History I
description: Any student enrolled in an Advanced Placement class must maintain a B average throughout the year in order to continue in that class, unless given special permission by the Supervisor. An Advanced Placement course is one that may be accepted for college credit at a number of participating colleges and universities upon the student’s successful completion of the Advanced Placement examination.
prereqText: Prerequisite: 9th Grade World History, placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: AP U.S. History II
description: Any student enrolled in an Advanced Placement class must maintain a B average throughout the year in order to continue in that class, unless given special permission by the Supervisor. An Advanced Placement course is one that may be accepted for college credit at a number of participating colleges and universities upon the student’s successful completion of the Advanced Placement examination. Year two of the AP U.S. History I & II sequence.

name: AP World History
description: The purpose of the AP World History course is to develop greater understanding of the evolution of global processes and contacts, in interaction with different types of human societies. This understanding is advanced through a combination of specific factual knowledge and appropriate analytical skills.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: AP Art History
description: Advanced Placement Art History is offered through the Social Studies Department as a rigorous, college-level humanities course that examines art as a lens for understanding global history, culture, and human expression. The course introduces students to the nature, function, and meaning of art across time, while emphasizing the connections between artistic production and historical context. Does not satisfy the Visual/Performing Arts requirement.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of Social Studies teacher and supervisor

name: Sociology
description: The purpose of this course is to give students an introduction to the field of sociology. Students will focus on social structure, patterns of culture, social class, deviance, mass media, and social problems.

name: AP Microeconomics
description: AP Microeconomics is an introductory college-level course that focuses on the principles of economics as they apply to individual consumers, firms, and markets. The course emphasizes the study of supply and demand, production and costs, market structures, factor markets, and the role of government in promoting economic efficiency and equity. Students must also take AP Macroeconomics.

name: AP Macroeconomics
description: AP Macroeconomics is an introductory college-level course that focuses on the principles that apply to an economic system as a whole. The course places particular emphasis on the study of national income and price-level determination; it also develops students' familiarity with economic performance measures, the financial sector, stabilization policies, economic growth, and international economics.

name: Constitutional Law
description: This course is designed to inform students about the American judicial system. Emphasis is placed on due process of law as expressed in the fourth, fifth, sixth, eighth, and fourteenth amendments to the U.S. Constitution. Students will explore and debate the reasoning of Supreme Court decisions and the ramifications of these decisions.

name: Religion in America
description: The major goals of this course are for students to learn the role that religion has played in the development of civilization and for them to understand how the religious experience of the American people has been affected by rapid economic, social, and political changes throughout history.

name: Critical Analysis of History Through Film
description: This elective will offer an opportunity for students to review concepts in American History through the study of film. The themes inherent in the U.S. I and U.S. II courses have been the subjects of many popular movies. Students will view these films in class and be asked to evaluate each in light of historical accuracy and the use of “poetic license.” 26

name: One World, One Community: World Problems Today
description: Students in this course will gain insight into a myriad of current world problems by examining multiple perspectives presented in newspapers, magazines, mass media, and the Internet. Topics such as environmental policies, population trends, world hunger, and the international war on drugs will be explored as students engage critically with primary and secondary sources.

name: Honors Psychology
description: The Psychology course gives students the opportunity to acquire quite possibly the most important life skills they will ever need: the ability to better understand themselves and others. The course establishes the fundamental principles of psychology and offers practical knowledge and techniques, in addition to important theories.
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Ramapo College.

name: An Introduction to the Analysis of Public Policy
description: Syracuse University Project Advance is a cooperative program between the Maxwell School of Public Affairs & Citizenship at Syracuse University and the Pascack Valley Regional High School District that allows high school seniors to enroll in a freshman-level college course. Must be taken together with AP American Government and Politics.
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Syracuse University Project Advance.

name: AP American Government and Politics
description: This course is designed to help students develop a working knowledge of the important concepts, theories, and facts of American government and politics. Coursework is calculated to prepare students for the Advanced Placement examination and includes the study of public policy, government institutions, political parties, interest groups, public opinion, mass media, and civil rights. Must be taken together with An Introduction to the Analysis of Public Policy.

name: History of Sport in America
description: This course traces the history of the USA from the standpoint of organized and professional sports across the decades. Students will be exposed to the economic, political, and social impacts of sports as they relate to the development of our country’s national identity. Topics include the impact of sports on race relations, gender issues, capitalism, globalization, regionalization and cultural identity.

name: Honors Geometry
description: In addition to covering the material from Geometry and Geometry Enhanced, Honors Geometry addresses additional topics and requires students to solve more challenging, non-routine problems.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of supervisor (based on 8th grade mathematics test/quiz averages, placement exam and teacher recommendation rubric)

name: Geometry Enhanced
description: In Geometry Enhanced, students study some topics in greater depth, and the pace of the course will be faster than in Geometry.
prereqText: Prerequisite: An initial test/quiz average of ‘C+’ or higher in 8th grade Algebra I; an initial test/quiz average of ‘B-’ or higher in 8th grade math Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: Geometry
description: In Geometry, students study the same concepts as in Geometry Enhanced, but with a greater emphasis on mastering prerequisite skills and a slightly slower pace.
prereqText: Prerequisite: A passing grade in 8th grade math

name: Algebra I Enhanced
description: The concepts presented in Algebra I courses are intended to extend and deepen the development of algebraic reasoning that began in middle school. In Algebra I Enhanced, students study some topics in greater depth, and the pace of the course will be faster than in Algebra I.
prereqText: Prerequisite: An initial test/quiz average of ‘C+’ or higher in Geometry Enhanced or ‘A’ or higher in Geometry Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: Algebra I
description: The concepts presented in Algebra I courses are intended to extend and deepen the development of algebraic reasoning that began in middle school. In Algebra I, students study the same concepts as in Algebra I Enhanced, but with a greater emphasis on mastering prerequisite skills and a slightly slower pace.
prereqText: Prerequisite: A passing grade in Geometry

name: Honors Algebra II with Trigonometry
description: In addition to covering the material from Algebra II with Trigonometry and Algebra II with Trigonometry Enhanced, Honors Algebra II with Trigonometry addresses additional topics and requires students to solve more challenging, non-routine problems. Graphing calculators are used regularly.
prereqText: Prerequisite: An initial test/quiz average of ‘B’ or higher in Honors Geometry; an initial test/quiz average of ‘A’ or higher in Geometry Enhanced and Algebra I Enhanced and proficiency on a placement exam Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: Algebra II with Trigonometry Enhanced
description: Algebra II with Trigonometry extends students’ understanding of functions and function families to include polynomial, rational, radical, and trigonometric functions. In Algebra II with Trigonometry Enhanced, students study some topics in greater depth, and the pace of the course will be faster.
prereqText: Prerequisite: An initial test/quiz average of ‘C+’ or higher in Algebra I Enhanced or ‘A’ or higher in Algebra I, and an initial test/quiz average of ‘C+’ or higher in Geometry Enhanced or ‘A’ or higher in Geometry Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: Algebra II with Trigonometry
description: Algebra II with Trigonometry extends students’ understanding of functions and function families to include polynomial, rational, radical, and trigonometric functions. Students study the same concepts as in the Enhanced course, with a greater emphasis on mastering prerequisite skills and a slightly slower pace.
prereqText: Prerequisite: A passing grade in Algebra I

name: Algebra II
description: In Algebra II, students solidify, strengthen, and extend their understanding of Algebra I and Geometry content.
prereqText: Prerequisite: A passing grade in Algebra I

name: College Algebra
description: This course provides students with a firm foundation on which to continue their study of mathematics in college. Topics will include algebraic operations, solutions of equations and inequalities, algebraic applications, functions, and trigonometry.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Algebra II with Trigonometry or Algebra II with Trigonometry Enhanced
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with William Paterson University.

name: AP Pre-Calculus
description: Advanced Placement Pre-Calculus covers the same material as Pre-Calculus, but the course moves at a quicker pace, and students will study many topics in greater depth. Students also begin their study of calculus towards the end of the year. Colleges may grant credit based upon the student’s score on the College Board’s Advanced Placement examination. Graphing calculators are used regularly throughout this course.
prereqText: Prerequisite: An initial test/quiz average of ‘B’ or higher in Honors Algebra II with Trigonometry; an initial test/quiz average of ‘A’ or higher in Algebra II with Trigonometry Enhanced and proficiency on a placement exam Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: Pre-Calculus
description: Pre-Calculus provides a firm foundation for study of mathematics at the college level. Students study more advanced functions, trigonometry, series and sequences, statistics, and limits. After completing this course, students will be prepared to take Calculus either at the high school or college level. Graphing calculators are used regularly throughout this course.
prereqText: Prerequisite: An initial test/quiz average of ‘B-’ or higher in Algebra II with Trigonometry Enhanced; an initial test/quiz average of ‘B+’ or higher in College Algebra and proficiency on a placement exam Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with William Paterson University.

name: AP Calculus BC
description: This full-year course investigates calculus from analytical, graphical, and numerical perspectives. The course builds on the function and limit theory introduced in Advanced Placement Pre-Calculus to fully develop the concept of the derivative and its applications. An investigation is then conducted into the concept of the integral, its use in solving differential equations, and its applications.
prereqText: Prerequisite: An initial test/quiz average of ‘B+’ or higher in Advanced Placement Pre-Calculus Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: AP Calculus AB
description: This full-year course covers all the material of Calculus in addition to a more in-depth study of integrals. Many colleges grant credit based upon the student’s score on the College Board’s Advanced Placement examination. Graphing calculators are used regularly throughout this course. Students are highly encouraged to take the AP exam in May.
prereqText: Prerequisite: An initial test/quiz average of ‘B-’ or higher in Advanced Placement Pre-Calculus; an initial test/quiz average of ‘A’ or higher in Pre-Calculus and proficiency on a placement exam Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: Calculus
description: This full-year course builds on students’ knowledge of functions and trigonometry to develop the concepts of calculus. Students will begin with a study of limit theory and use that to fully develop the concept of the derivative. Students will study the derivative from analytical, graphical, and numerical perspectives and investigate its applications.
prereqText: Prerequisite: An initial test/quiz average of ‘B-’ or higher in Pre-Calculus
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with William Paterson University.

name: Advanced Topics in Calculus (Honors)
description: This full-year course will extend key ideas of one- variable calculus to functions with several variables. Topics will include the three-dimensional coordinate system, vectors, equations of lines, planes, cylinders, and quadric surfaces in three- dimensional space, vector functions and their applications to arc length, curvature, and motion in space, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and theorems of vector...
prereqText: Prerequisite: Successful completion of Advanced Placement Calculus BC Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with William Paterson University.

name: Statistics
description: This course will prepare students to collect and analyze data for the purpose of making determinations on typical values and variation. Students will learn to model data sets in order to draw conclusions and make predictions, and compute probabilities and run simulations for situations where probabilities cannot be computed.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Algebra II with Trigonometry or Algebra II with Trigonometry Enhanced
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with William Paterson University.

name: AP Statistics
description: This is a full-year, non-calculus-based statistics course that is typically required as part of a student’s work in engineering, sociology, psychology, health, the sciences, and business. The course will cover a) the exploratory analysis of data, b) the planning of a study, c) the production of models using probability theory and simulation, and d) the use of statistical inference.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Algebra II with Trigonometry Enhanced or College Algebra with an initial test/quiz average of ‘B+’ or higher Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: Discrete Math
description: This course is designed to develop the quantitative reasoning skills that students will need for their daily lives and futures. The course will emphasize deep conceptual understanding of real-world applications, and topics may include banking, taxes, loans, investments, and credit cards.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Algebra II with Trigonometry
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with William Paterson University.

name: Introduction to Computer Science and App Development
description: Introduction to Computer Science and App Development offers a multidisciplinary approach to the creative aspects of programming, abstractions, algorithms, large data sets, the Internet, cybersecurity concerns, and computing impacts.
prereqText: Co-requisite or Prerequisite: Geometry or Geometry Enhanced

name: Honors Computer Science
description: In this full-year elective course students will learn the fundamentals of computer programming in Java, with an emphasis on the development of logical thinking and problem-solving skills.
prereqText: Co-requisite or Prerequisite: Honors Algebra II with Trigonometry or Algebra II with Trigonometry Enhanced and a high level of interest in programming, or Intro to Computer Science and App Development Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: AP Computer Science A
description: The Advanced Placement Computer Science A course is equivalent to a first-semester, college-level course in computer science.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Honors Computer Science Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: Advanced Topics in Computer Science (Honors)
description: Advanced Topics in Computer Science (Honors) requires a strong background in computer programming. It emphasizes problem solving, procedural and data abstraction, programming and design methodology, and algorithm analysis through a project-based approach.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Successful completion of Advanced Placement Computer Science A Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: Math 8
description: Eighth grade mathematics. Reference only, not plannable.

name: Algebra I (8th grade)
description: Algebra I taken in 8th grade. Reference only, not plannable.

name: Pre-Algebra (8th grade)
description: Pre-Algebra taken in 8th grade. Reference only, not plannable.

name: Biology
description: This college preparatory course provides students with a solid foundation in the major concepts of biology at a pace that allows for extensive practice, reinforcement, and guided support. Students explore biochemistry, cell structure and processes, genetics, evolution, and ecology through phenomenon-based instruction and real-world applications.

name: Biology Enhanced
description: Biology Enhanced is a more rigorous college preparatory course for students ready to engage more deeply with biological concepts while still benefiting from structured support. Students study biochemistry, cell processes, genetics, evolution, and ecology through phenomenon-based learning, real-world problem solving, and hands-on laboratory experiences.

name: Honors Biology
description: Honors Biology is a fast-paced, highly rigorous course designed for students with strong analytical skills and the ability to learn with greater independence. Students investigate biochemistry, cell processes, genetics, evolution, and ecology through inquiry-driven labs, real- world phenomena, and complex problem-solving tasks. Transcripts have shown 6 credits for this honors course. The catalog lists 5 until a counselor confirms.
prereqText: Suggested Co-requisite: Honors Geometry or Geometry Enhanced

name: AP Biology
description: This course is equivalent to an introductory college course in biology. Major points of emphasis are molecular biology, biotechnology, energy transfer, cells, ecology, biochemistry, botany, anatomy and physiology, genetics, and microbiology. There is extensive laboratory work, plus readings outside of class focusing on biological issues.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor Co-requisite or Prerequisite: Honors Chemistry, Honors Physics

name: Chemistry
description: This college preparatory course provides students with a solid foundation in the fundamental concepts of chemistry at a pace that allows for greater practice, support, and reinforcement.
prereqText: Suggested Co-requisite: Algebra I

name: Chemistry Enhanced
description: Chemistry Enhanced is a challenging college preparatory course designed for students who are ready to engage more deeply with chemistry concepts while still benefiting from guided practice and structured support.
prereqText: Suggested Co-requisite: Algebra I Enhanced

name: Honors Chemistry
description: Honors Chemistry is an accelerated and highly rigorous laboratory science course designed for students with strong math and analytical skills. Transcripts have shown 6 credits for this honors course. The catalog lists 5 until a counselor confirms.
prereqText: Prerequisite: ‘B’ or better in Honors Biology OR an ‘A’ in Biology Enhanced. Students who have not completed Algebra I will also have to complete a math skills placement test prior to final placement decision. Suggested Co-requisite: Honors Algebra II with Trigonometry or Algebra II with Trigonometry Enhanced

name: AP Chemistry
description: This course is comparable to an introductory course in chemistry at the college level. Students study the following topics: 1) the structure and states of matter, 2) chemical bonding; 3) thermodynamics; 4) chemical reactions; 5) solutions; 6) kinetics; 7) acids and bases; 8) redox; and 9) equilibrium.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor Prerequisite: Grade of ‘B’ or better in Honors Chemistry Co-requisite or prerequisite: Honors Physics/AP Physics I

name: Physics
description: This college preparatory course provides students with a strong introduction to the fundamental principles of physics at a pace that allows for guided practice, reinforcement, and skill-building. Students explore momentum, energy, earth science concepts, DC circuits, electromagnetism, waves, and space science through phenomenon-based learning, real-world applications, and hands-on laboratory investigations.
prereqText: Co-requisite: Algebra II with Trigonometry

name: Physics Enhanced
description: Physics Enhanced is a more rigorous college preparatory course for students who are ready to engage more deeply with physics concepts while still benefiting from structured support.
prereqText: Suggested Co-requisite: Algebra II with Trigonometry Enhanced or Honors Algebra II with Trigonometry

name: Honors Physics
description: Honors Physics is a rigorous, fast-paced course designed for students with strong mathematical reasoning skills and the ability to learn with a high level of independence. Students explore momentum, energy, earth science, DC circuits, electromagnetism, waves, and space science through inquiry-driven labs, complex problem-solving tasks, and phenomenon-based investigations.
prereqText: Prerequisite: ‘B’ or better in Honors Chemistry OR an ‘A’ in Chemistry Enhanced Suggested Co-requisite: AP Pre-Calculus, Pre-Calculus, or Calculus

name: AP Physics I
description: This course is equivalent to an introductory college course in non-calculus-based physics and is designed to prepare students for the AP Physics I exam. This course is designed to be equivalent to physics courses required for students majoring in the life sciences, pre-medicine, and other applied science fields.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor Co-requisite: AP Pre-Calculus, Pre-Calculus, or Calculus

name: Applied Physics & Engineering
description: Applied Physics & Engineering is a full-year, ten-credit course, taught by a physics instructor and a technology instructor. The course is designed to emphasize physical concepts that are applicable to technology, and to incorporate these concepts into working technological prototypes. Two-period, 10-credit course. Fulfills the physics graduation requirement. The PDF lists two different prerequisites.
prereqText: Science Department listing: Prerequisite: Algebra I. Technology Education listing: Prerequisite: Chemistry

name: AP Physics II
description: This course is equivalent to an introductory college course in non-calculus-based physics and is designed to prepare students for the AP Physics 2 exam. Students explore principles of fluids, thermodynamics, electricity, magnetism, optics, and topics in modern physics. There is extensive laboratory work, plus readings outside of class focusing on physics-related issues.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor Prerequisite: Grade of ‘B’ or better in Honors Physics/AP Physics I

name: AP Physics C
description: This course is equivalent to an introductory college course in calculus-based physics and is designed to prepare students for the AP Physics C exam. Students explore principles of mechanics and electricity and magnetism. There is extensive laboratory work, plus readings outside of class focusing on physics-related issues.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor Prerequisite: Grade of ‘B’ or better in Honors Physics/AP Physics I Co-requisite: Calculus

name: Science, Ethics, Technology and Society
description: In this course, students will examine controversial/ethical issues and advances in technology over time, and their impact on the way we live and the way our society is structured.

name: Honors Forensic Science
description: Forensic Science is focused upon the application of scientific methods and techniques to crime and law. This course is intended to introduce the science behind crime detection. Scientific methods specifically relevant to crime detection and analysis will be presented with emphasis placed upon the techniques used in evaluating physical evidence.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor Prerequisite: Successful Completion of Biology, Chemistry, and Physics
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Syracuse University (4 college credits).

name: Honors Research in Molecular Genetics I
description: This is an honors-level advanced research program that is formulated to reflect the skills, behaviors, techniques, and proficiencies necessary for conducting authentic science research. Students will learn how to analyze and interpret experimental data generated in class and by other researchers.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor Prerequisite: Honors Biology or a grade of ‘A-’ or better in Biology Enhanced

name: Honors Research in Molecular Genetics II
description: This is an honors-level advanced research program that is designed to allow students to design and carry out their own, authentic research. The authentic research experience will require students to work closely with an expert or mentor in the particular field of research.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor Prerequisite: Research in Molecular Genetics I and Research in Molecular Genetics II for RMG III Grades 11, 12

name: Honors Research in Molecular Genetics III
description: This is an honors-level advanced research program that is designed to allow students to design and carry out their own, authentic research. The authentic research experience will require students to work closely with an expert or mentor in the particular field of research.
prereqText: Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor Prerequisite: Research in Molecular Genetics I and Research in Molecular Genetics II for RMG III Grades 11, 12

name: Introduction to Anatomy and Physiology
description: The Introduction to Anatomy and Physiology course covers the basics of anatomy and physiology including anatomical terminology, basic biochemistry, cells and tissues, and the study of the major organ systems of various species in both healthy and diseased states. The course will involve laboratory activities/dissections, models, diagrams, journal writings, text material and clinical studies.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Grade of ‘C’ or better in a biology course

name: Honors Anatomy and Physiology
description: In this course, students will conduct an in-depth and detailed study of the major organ systems of various species in both healthy and diseased states, including morphology and functional features of the cells and tissues. As part of each unit of study, students will research and present case-based medical scenarios utilizing a variety of multimedia applications.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Honors Biology or a grade of an ‘A-’ or better in Biology Enhanced Placement by recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: Astronomy
description: This semester-long science elective will be a descriptive survey of key topics in astronomy. This course will investigate the history of modern astronomy, discuss astronomy-related technologies of ancient civilizations, and progress to modern astronomical observatories and telescopes.

name: Earth’s Natural Disasters
description: This semester-long science elective will be a descriptive survey of key natural disasters. This course will investigate destructive forces involved in geology, meteorology and geography. Topics will examine the natural as well as the human consequences of earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, tornadoes, hurricanes, wildfires, meteor impacts and other natural events.

name: AP Environmental Science
description: The Advanced Placement Environmental Science course is designed to be the equivalent of a one-semester, introductory college course in environmental science, through which students engage with the scientific principles, concepts, and methodologies required to understand the interrelationships of the natural world.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Chemistry or Honors Chemistry Co-requisite or prerequisite: Chemistry Enhanced or Physics Enhanced

name: Chinese I
description: This course is designed for novice students who begin without knowledge of the target language. The emphasis of the course is on real-life communication. Students will be given the opportunity to acquire and interact in the language, as it is spoken and written in the target culture.

name: Chinese II
description: At Language II levels, communication skills are reinforced and further developed. There is an additional concentration on reading and writing. Also included are studies of vocabulary and idiom development, as well as some study of the history and culture of the country (countries) whose language is being studied.

name: Chinese III
description: At Language III levels, there is an increased reinforcement and development of communication skills already introduced in Levels I and II. Additional emphasis is placed on the ongoing development of reading and writing skills, as well as more in-depth presentations of target structures, vocabulary, and idioms.

name: Chinese IV
description: At upper levels, the goals are essentially similar to those of Level III, although a higher level of ability in the language is expected. In addition to continued emphasis on communication skills, there is an introduction to authentic literature in the language being studied. Review of previously taught linguistic structures, oral recitation, extensive vocabulary and idiom development, and composition are included.
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Seton Hall University.

name: Chinese V
description: At upper levels, the goals are essentially similar to those of Level III, although a higher level of ability in the language is expected. In addition to continued emphasis on communication skills, there is an introduction to authentic literature in the language being studied. Review of previously taught linguistic structures, oral recitation, extensive vocabulary and idiom development, and composition are included.
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Seton Hall University.

name: Honors Chinese II
description: The honors program is designed for students who demonstrate a high level of ability in oral and written expression, and who are motivated to achieve an advanced level of proficiency. In the honors program, students will be expected to achieve a strong command of the target language, which includes accurate usage of target structures and extensive application of vocabulary and idiomatic expressions.
