dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Seton Hall University.

name: AP Spanish Literature and Culture
description: This course is designed to provide students with a learning experience equivalent to that of an introductory college course in literature written in Spanish. The course introduces students to the formal study of a representative body of texts from Peninsular Spanish, Latin American, and U.S. Hispanic literature.
prereqText: Prerequisite: AP Spanish Language & Culture or Spanish for Heritage Speakers III, recommendation of teacher and supervisor

name: Spanish for Heritage Speakers I
description: Spanish for Heritage Speakers I, II & III are proficiency-based courses which involve meaningful use of language for real communicative purposes. Instruction focuses on what students can do with the language and build upon their L1 literacy skills, specifically reading comprehension and their written expression. Students entering the program should speak Spanish at home on a regular basis with their families. Honors designation and course credit are available to eligible students.

name: Spanish for Heritage Speakers II
description: Spanish for Heritage Speakers I, II & III are proficiency-based courses which involve meaningful use of language for real communicative purposes. Instruction focuses on what students can do with the language and build upon their L1 literacy skills, specifically reading comprehension and their written expression. Students entering the program should speak Spanish at home on a regular basis with their families. Honors designation and course credit are available to eligible students.

name: Spanish for Heritage Speakers III
description: Spanish for Heritage Speakers I, II & III are proficiency-based courses which involve meaningful use of language for real communicative purposes. Instruction focuses on what students can do with the language and build upon their L1 literacy skills, specifically reading comprehension and their written expression. Students entering the program should speak Spanish at home on a regular basis with their families. Honors designation and course credit are available to eligible students.

name: English Language Development
description: English Language Development is a special course designed to teach English to students whose native language is one other than English. As in learning any of the world languages taught in the Pascack Valley Regional High School District, the method of instruction is a communicative approach emphasizing the four basic communication skills: (1) listening and understanding; (2) speaking; (3) reading; and (4) writing.

name: Studio Art I
description: Studio Art I is an entry-level course in visual communication where students can explore various media and techniques for self-expression. Students will engage in a variety of visual problem- solving experiences and skills such as drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture and mixed media. Projects will have a strong focus on the elements and principles of art and design.

name: Honors Advanced Studio Art II
description: Studio Art II as an extension of Studio Art I. Student work will be expanded to deal with visual problems and personal interpretations. The work will focus on the refinement of technical skills in the areas of drawing, painting, printmaking and mixed media. This is a “portfolio preparation” course for the development of personal, college, and/or Advanced Placement Art in Drawing or 2- Dimensional Design portfolio. 49
prereqText: Prerequisite: Studio Art I AND Teacher Approved Portfolio/Recommendation

name: Ceramics & Sculpture I
description: Students who like to work with their hands will enjoy this opportunity to design with plaster, wood, clay and mixed media. Students will learn the secrets and strategies used by artists over the centuries. They will use pinch, coil and slab methods and become familiar with using the potter’s wheel as well as learning methods in wood, plaster and stone.

name: Honors Advanced Ceramics & Sculpture II
description: The purpose of this class is to prepare students for self-directed advanced studio work in clay and mixed media sculpture materials. Students will be prepared to work in a personal studio career, or continued education in ceramics.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Ceramics & Sculpture I AND Teacher Approved Portfolio/Recommendation

name: Photography I
description: This is an introductory studio course in which students become familiar with the fundamentals of photography. Students look at their world as it is composed through the lens of the camera. Students will learn how to use the creative controls of the camera to better express themselves visually.

name: Honors Advanced Photography II
description: This course is designed for students who have successfully completed the introductory photography course. Students will have the opportunity to apply previously learned techniques and procedures to more in-depth photographic study.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Photography I AND Teacher Approved Portfolio/Recommendation

name: Communication Design
description: This course is designed for students who have completed a 100-level course of a hands-on arts elective and could use an intermediate art-making experience (as opposed to, in addition to, or before taking the Honors Advanced /AP level courses).
prereqText: Prerequisite: Photography I and/or teacher recommendation

name: AP Drawing
description: For this course, students focus on mastering the art of drawing through a wide range of experiences, including drawing techniques, use of drawing media, subject matter and the development of a personal approach to art making. In addition to traditional approaches to drawing, media such as painting, printmaking, and mixed media can be explored and included in this portfolio. Grades are not stated in the PDF.

name: AP 2-D Art and Design
description: In this course, students will focus on work in a variety of media: drawing, painting, printmaking, photography, craft, and digital imaging (all 2-dimensional art activities). The course is designed to guide each student’s growth and personal development in the visual arts. Grades are not stated in the PDF.

name: AP 3-D Art and Design
description: This course will investigate styles, techniques and historical movements in sculpture and is designed as an intensive one-year program that challenges students’ creativity and design skills. The course enables students to develop a body of work that investigates strong underlying visual ideas in 3-D design. Grades are not stated in the PDF.

name: Financial Literacy
description: Decisions about how to spend and invest money are lifelong skills and very important to our financial future. This course is designed to develop personal strategies in banking, credit, investing, buying or leasing an automobile, buying insurance, purchasing a house and planning for a major event.

name: Financial Literacy (Hybrid)
description: The Hybrid Financial Literacy course option is a hybrid of the PVRHSD Financial Literacy course. The program includes the same core material as the classroom option listed above but with limited teacher/student contact (approximately six-to-ten face to face meetings per semester with weekly online interactions). Online hybrid option that fulfills the same requirement.

name: Principles of Business
description: The world of business is a dynamic environment where the only constant is an ever-changing global landscape. Businesspersons need to be skilled in dealing with diversity, promoting ethics and social responsibility, sustaining customer relationships, understanding the impact of government regulation on business, finance and accounting, marketing, and the importance of e-commerce.

name: Entrepreneurship
description: Using various entrepreneurial models, the students work as team members in a simulated business environment within the high school setting. The course is designed to familiarize students with the world of small business and provide opportunities to analyze the personal strengths and weaknesses of individuals who have launched a career in entrepreneurship.

name: Marketing
description: The Marketing Course focuses on concepts in effectively marketing goods and services to customers from a domestic and global perspective. The course includes market research, identifying target customers, developing product offers, branding, pricing, marketing communications, and distribution.

name: Management and Leadership
description: Management and Leadership is a half-year course that is available to students in grades 10-12, who have successfully completed at least one business class. This course explores essential skills and knowledge needed to become highly qualified business professionals in today’s technological business environment.
prereqText: Prerequisite: One Business Course

name: Honors Marketing and Merchandising
description: Students accepted into the honors level course must have completed two years of business courses (through half-ear or full-year opportunities) and must have the teacher recommendation. The Honors level marketing course dives deeper into the Marketing Mix: planning, advertising, merchandising, sales, and promotion. Several units will discuss Social Media/Content Marketing and Digital Marketing.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Marketing and Principles of Business

name: Financial Investment
description: The goal of the half-year Financial Investment course is to educate and extend student knowledge of financial responsibility and the practice of sound investing strategies. The course will focus on the diverse investment strategies individuals use to seek out a positive return. The course will require that students explore topics of how corporate finance works and the corporate structures of businesses.

name: Accounting
description: Accounting is a full-year accelerated course where students will learn how to record, analyze, interpret, and report financial information in a manual and computerized environment. This course is taught using a college-level textbook and covers material similar to a college accounting course. QuickBooks software, Excel, and Google Sheets spreadsheet applications will be utilized.

name: Career Exploration (Internship)
description: The Career Exploration Internship Program (Senior Experience) is a 15-credit, full-year, half- day immersive learning experience designed to connect classroom learning with authentic professional practice. Senior half-day program worth 15 credits.

name: Honors Teacher Cadet Program
description: The Center for Educator Recruitment, Retention, and Advancement’s (CERRA) nationally recognized Teacher Cadet Program is an innovative, curriculum-based college level course designed to attract talented young people to the education profession through a challenging introduction to teaching.

name: Teacher Assistant Program
description: Goal: To give students the opportunity to work within a department or subject area of the school as a Teaching Assistant (“TA”) in order to give them additional exposure to a subject they are interested in and to support the teaching and learning in the class. Eligibility: 11th or 12th grade student who has previously taken the course they wish to TA in with a grade of B or higher. Worth 2.5 or 5 credits depending on the length of the course. Does not fulfill any State requirement.

name: 21st Century Life Skills
description: Students will participate in a variety of experiences including techniques in nutritional planning, food preparation, basic clothing design and construction, and investigations into the relationship dynamics of a family/community. Students will also explore budgeting, future careers, planning for an interview, and enhancing communication skills.

name: Culinary Arts I
description: Basic food preparation skills and techniques will be developed and applied to real-life situations. Food choices are influenced by such factors as available resources, family customs, cultural traditions, religious customs, friends, advertising, and current trends and lifestyles.

name: Culinary Arts II
description: This laboratory course is open to those students interested in learning advanced techniques of food preparation. Emphasis is placed on critically evaluating one's work, understanding reasons for success and failure, food presentation, and recipe development. Quantity food preparation, the study of international foods, and current trends in the culinary field are also part of the program.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Culinary Arts I

name: Clothing Construction
description: This course is designed for students interested in learning how to construct their own garments. The elements and principles of design are utilized in selecting and constructing attractive fashions. The students learn how to care for and use various types of sewing equipment, including the sewing machine.

name: Advanced Clothing Construction
description: Students interested in learning advanced clothing construction techniques will find this course desirable. Changing commercial patterns and/or working from one's original design are part of the program. A basic knowledge of sewing is necessary.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Clothing Construction

name: Fashion Design
description: This course presents an overview of the historical development of fashion as it is related to current design. Students will develop the skill of drawing the figure, designing for specific figure variations, coordinating accessory design, and studying fashion trends in textiles. Students have the opportunity to design and construct complete outfits from drawing to finished product by the end of the year.

name: Advanced Fashion Design
description: This course is designed for students who wish to further their depth of knowledge and skills in the fashion areas. The elements of design are emphasized and transferred into flat pattern or draping and the creation of a finished garment. Special fabrics and advanced construction techniques will be emphasized. Students will develop a professional portfolio to be used for entrance requirements to schools.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Fashion Design

name: Interior Design
description: This course is designed for students who are interested in learning the fundamental elements and principles of design related to housing and Interior Design. Elements and principles of design, apartment living, housing styles, evaluating floor plans, financial considerations related to housing, furniture styles, and physical treatments of rooms are some of the areas studied.

name: Early Childhood and Family Education I
description: This is a hands-on laboratory course that has specific qualifications for students to be enrolled: • Students must be of excellent character as they serve as the role models for preschool children to exemplify and emulate. • Students must be dependable, reliable, and with outstanding school attendance.

name: Early Childhood and Family Education II
description: Early Childhood and Family Education II is an advanced course designed and recommended for the student who is interested in the field of Early Childhood Education, Psychology, Special Education, Social Work, and other related careers. Topics include curriculum areas in preschool education, planning developmentally appropriate learning activities for the preschool child, and practice with caring for young children.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Early Childhood and Family Education I

name: Early Childhood and Family Education III
description: Early Childhood and Family Education III is designed for the student who plans to work and study in the field of early childhood education, social work, or psychology. Students will further their understanding of developing age-appropriate lessons and teaching these lessons to preschool-aged children.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Early Childhood and Family Education II

name: Daily Food Preparation and Nutrition Skills
description: The Daily Food Preparation and Nutrition Skills course is designed to assist students within the Pascack Valley Regional High School District to acquire food selection, handling, and nutrition skills necessary for living on their own after high school. Students will also learn proper table setting and etiquette practices.

name: Physical Education/Health 9
description: Combined Physical Education and Health Education. New Jersey requires 150 minutes of Physical Education/Health & Safety per week.

name: Physical Education/Driver Ed 10
description: Combined Physical Education and Health Education. New Jersey requires 150 minutes of Physical Education/Health & Safety per week. Includes driver and traffic safety education.

name: Physical Education/Health 11
description: Combined Physical Education and Health Education. New Jersey requires 150 minutes of Physical Education/Health & Safety per week.

name: Physical Education/Health 12
description: Combined Physical Education and Health Education. New Jersey requires 150 minutes of Physical Education/Health & Safety per week.

name: Choir/Lunch
description: This choral class meets for a half period and is designed so all students can have a choral experience. Students will learn proper vocal technique as well as perform music of all genres. Performances throughout the year are presented with other vocal ensembles. Meets for a half period. The 2.5 credit value is unverified.

name: Concert Choir
description: Membership in the Concert Choir is open to all high school students, regardless of any previous musical background or experience. Concert Choir meets for a full period and provides students with a more in-depth experience. The course concentrates on vocal training, performance, and sight-reading skills. Students perform throughout the year with exposure to a variety of music styles.

name: Chamber Choir
description: Chamber Choir is our most advanced choral ensemble. The goal of this choir is to enrich vocal technique, performance standards, and sight-reading skills. The music performed is designed to challenge the student vocalist. The repertoire comes from all genres of music with performances occurring throughout the year. Selection to this ensemble is by audition with the Choral Director at the high school.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Audition*
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Seton Hall University.

name: Honors Chamber Choir
description: Honors Chamber Choir is an advanced, audition-based course for dedicated vocalists in grades 10–12 who have participated in choir throughout high school and are concurrently enrolled in Chamber Choir. This rigorous program is designed to foster individual musical growth, leadership, and academic excellence through high-level study and performance.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Audition

name: Concert Band
description: Membership in the Concert Band will be open to all high school students, regardless of any previous musical background or experience, interested in learning to play a brass, woodwind, or percussion instrument. The Concert Band program includes music fundamentals of reading music notation, performance techniques, and rules of music interpretation.
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Seton Hall University.

name: Honors Concert Band
description: This course is designed to deepen musical and academic growth, and the honors band program emphasizes leadership, performance excellence, and independent study. Students in Honors Concert Band engage in advanced work such as developing a performance portfolio, maintaining a practice journal, conducting performance-related research, and participating in additional lessons and advanced performance opportunities.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Audition

name: Modern Rock Band
description: Modern Rock Band is open to all students in grades 9-12 who are interested in a non-traditional band experience. No prior classical music training is necessary for this class, and students will be exposed to the core instrumentation of the Drum Set, Bass Guitar, Electric Guitar, and Keyboard. Experience in this genre and collection of instruments is not needed but certainly welcomed.

name: Keyboard/Piano
description: The keyboard/piano course is a performance-based class for those students who are interested in learning to play piano/keyboard or seeking to improve their keyboard skills. The class is open to students from beginner to advanced level. No audition is required to be accepted to this class. Each student will develop a repertoire of piano pieces that will be suitable to their level.

name: Music Technology
description: This course is designed for students interested in exploring the world of music technology. Music technology will equip students with a working knowledge of the industry tools for composition and notation, sound recording/engineering, web presence development, and the history of commercial music in the United States.
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Seton Hall University.

name: Music Theory
description: This course is recommended for students with a serious interest in music, or those planning a music major or minor in college. This course is designed for students who seek the opportunity to study music theory, write original compositions, or plan to continue their study of music in college.

name: AP Music Theory
description: This course is recommended for students with a serious interest in music, or those planning a music major or minor in college. It will also prepare students to take the AP Music Theory exam in May. This course is designed for students who seek the opportunity to recognize, understand, and describe the materials and processes of music that are heard or created in a score.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Recommendation of teacher and supervisor
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with Seton Hall University.

name: Guitar I
description: This class is open to all students interested in studying music and playing the guitar regardless of their musical background. The Guitar I class introduces the fundamentals of guitar playing through a variety of musical styles, time periods, and levels of complexity. It includes interpreting music for the guitar, chord symbols, music reading, and the utilization of various finger picks and strums.

name: American Pop Music
description: This course is designed for students who seek the opportunity to extend their musical understanding, heighten their music listening skills, and increase their ability to respond more fully to music by tracing the development of American Music to the present.

name: Creative Design Principles in STEM
description: This course introduces students to principles in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math) and Design. Students will learn how computer software and rapid prototyping processes, such as 3D printing, can be used to design and create products, ranging from car parts and smartphone cases to graphics, fashion accessories, and prosthetics.

name: Graphic Design I
description: This course will introduce students to the concepts of using graphic images to communicate information and ideas, sell products, and influence public opinion.

name: Graphic Design II
description: In this course, students will build upon the skills developed in Graphic Design I as they continue to combine technology and art to communicate ideas visually and explore career paths in graphic design.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Graphic Design I

name: Architecture
description: In this STEM and design course, students will integrate the design process as it relates to creating a 3-D model of a residential structure (i.e. a dream home). They will learn to develop floor plans, cross-sections, elevations, and perspective drawings, and the fundamental concepts related to communicating architecture-related technical information and design ideas.

name: Robotics and Game Design
description: In this STEM and design course, students will explore the fields of robotics, control systems, and game design, using various computer programs and applications. Students will work individually and in teams to design, program, build, and test robotics systems and games. Students will integrate engineering design and computer programming to solve design challenges and bring their ideas to life. DUAL ENROLLMENT OPTION

name: Honors Engineering Design I
description: In this STEM and design course, students will identify problems, perform research, and conceive and design solutions in a variety of engineering disciplines, including but not limited to chemical, civil, computer, electrical, industrial, mechanical, reverse, and systems engineering while exploring Universal Design.
prereqText: Co-requisite for 9th grade students: Honors Biology
dualEnrollmentNote: Dual enrollment option with the University of Texas at Austin.

name: Honors Engineering Design II
description: After taking Engineering Design I, students will have the opportunity to hone their STEM and design abilities and apply them to more complex engineering problems. Taking on the role of engineer, students will identify problems, perform research, and conceive and design solutions in a variety of engineering disciplines, as well as enter local competitions. Fulfills the physics graduation requirement.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Engineering Design I

name: Video Production
description: Video Production is designed to give students basic instruction and hands-on experience in the operation of the various kinds of equipment typically found in commercial television studio and film sets. Students will be directly involved in planning, shooting, and editing various projects throughout the year including music videos, short films, commercials, and more.

name: Advanced Video Production
description: Advanced Video Production is designed to review, expand upon, and apply the basic operational techniques introduced in Video Production. Students will learn how to use professional cameras (DSLR and Television Studio Cameras) and expand their editing IQ using After Effects.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Successful completion of Video Production and teacher recommendation

name: Honors Broadcast Television Production
description: Students will learn advanced studio and field production techniques, including the use of professional equipment and software as they apply to individual projects, as well as the school- based news shows. This course includes production and development of content for the weekly news shows. Students will interview staff and students and film academic, extracurricular, and athletic events.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Successful completion of Video Production and teacher recommendation

name: Honors Research in Innovation and Design
description: In this capstone course, students will carry out an independent project of their own design. They will submit their work to regional and state competitions for opportunities to compete at the national and international level.
prereqText: Prerequisite: Successful completion of one or more Technology Education courses and teacher recommendation

name: Satellite School
description: The Bergen County Technical Education Center, Northeast Satellite School in Paramus is a shared-time facility that cooperates with local high schools in Northern Bergen County. Paramus Satellite provides local high schools with County-sponsored vocational-technical courses directed to the individual needs of job-oriented high school students. Credit value is not stated in the PDF. Confirm with a counselor.

name: Virtual High School (VHS)
description: Virtual High School is a collaborative of more than 200 high schools from across the country and around the world. It offers students a way to experience fully virtual learning. A student should consider taking a VHS class only if they are an extremely self-motivated, self-disciplined learner who is a proficient user of technology. VHS allows students an opportunity to pursue an area of particular interest. Credit value is not stated in the PDF. Confirm with a counselor.

name: Study Skills
description: Study Skills provides supplemental support to students across the curriculum, to meet the NJSLS as designated in the district's curriculum guides for English, Math, Science, Social Studies, and World Language.

name: English 1-2 and 3-4
description: In English 1, 2, 3, and 4, an individual prescriptive approach is infused into instruction to address language arts skills that will more effectively prepare students to pursue life goals. The ultimate purpose is to develop literate readers, writers, speakers, listeners, and viewers. The primary teaching goal is to strengthen each student’s ability to understand, process, and communicate information. Credit value is not stated in the PDF. Confirm with a counselor.

name: Themes in World History
description: In Themes in World History, students will acquire the knowledge and skills to think analytically and systematically about how past interactions of people, cultures, and the environment affect issues across time and cultures. Such knowledge and skills enable students to make informed decisions as socially and ethically responsible world citizens in the 21st century.

name: Themes in United States History I
description: In Themes in United States History I, students will acquire the knowledge and skills to think analytically and systematically about how past interactions of people, cultures, and the environment affect issues across time and cultures. Such knowledge and skills enable students to make informed decisions as socially and ethically responsible world citizens in the 21st century.

name: Themes in United States History II
description: In Themes in United States History II, students will acquire the knowledge and skills to think analytically and systematically about how past interactions of people, cultures, and the environment affect issues across time and cultures. Such knowledge and skills enable students to make informed decisions as socially and ethically responsible world citizens in the 21st century.

name: Math 1-2 and 3-4
description: In Math 1, 2, 3 and 4, students will demonstrate increasingly complex understanding of number sense, spatial reasoning, geometric principles, measurement, data, personal finance, and analytic procedures. Students will solve increasingly complex mathematical problems, making productive use of algebra and functions. Credit value is not stated in the PDF. Confirm with a counselor.

name: Elements of Biological Science
description: Grade 9 or 10 This course is designed to give students an understanding of science practices in the field of biology. The intent of this course is to provide each student the opportunity to develop an understanding and appreciation of major scientific concepts including cell processes, genetics, evolution, and ecology.

name: Elements of Chemistry in the Community
description: Grade 9 or 10 This course is designed to give students an understanding of some of the key aspects and applications of chemistry.

name: Elements of Conceptual Physics
description: Grade 11 or 12 This course is designed to give students an understanding of some of the key aspects and applications of physics. The intent of this course is to provide each student the opportunity to acquire knowledge of major scientific concepts.

name: Elements of Science 1
description: Grade 9 or 10 Designed to instill a strong foundation in science and engineering, the Elements of Science 1 course offers students an immersive exploration of key concepts in life science, physical science, and earth and space science.

name: Elements of Science 2
description: Grade 9 or 10 Continuing the journey from Elements of Science 1, the Elements of Science 2 course propels students further into the wonders of science, building upon foundational skills acquired in the previous class. With a focus on chemical reactions, natural selection, and environmental conservation, students will engage in hands-on explorations while continuing to develop critical thinking skills.

name: Elements of Science 3
description: Grade 10 or 11 Elements of Science 3 builds upon the solid foundation established in the preceding courses. This class delves into three captivating topics: body systems, collisions and force, and conservation.

name: Elements of Innovation and Design
description: This course introduces students to principles in STEM (Science Technology Engineering and Math) and Design. Students will learn how computer software and rapid prototyping processes, such as 3D printing, can be used to design and create products, ranging from car parts and smartphone cases to graphics, fashion accessories, and prosthetics.

name: Spanish Conversation & Culture
description: This is an introductory-level course designed to engage students in meaningful, real-world communication while exploring the rich diversity of Spanish-speaking cultures. Through interactive activities, songs, projects, and visuals, students will build foundational language skills to greet others, talk about themselves, describe their surroundings, and express likes and feelings.

name: Transition Education 1 and 2
description: This course focuses on instruction and support services needed to help students move from the school environment to the workforce, vocational program, or other program designed to promote independent living. Concurrently, students participate in Job Sampling and Structured Learning Experiences. Through Job Sampling, students are introduced to professions and industries to help them prepare for employment. Credit value is not stated in the PDF. Confirm with a counselor.

name: Daily Living Skills 1 and 2
description: The Daily Living Skills 1 and 2 course is designed to provide each student the opportunity to acquire knowledge in the areas of independent living, including functional life and social skills. Community-Based Instruction is a component of the Daily Living Skills curriculum that helps students generalize classroom-based learning in community settings. Credit value is not stated in the PDF. Confirm with a counselor.

name: Related Arts
description: Related Arts is an entry-level course in visual communication where students can explore various media and techniques for self-expression. Students will engage in a variety of visual problem- solving experiences and skills such as drawing, painting, printmaking, photography, sculpture, ceramics, and mixed media. Projects will have a strong focus on the elements and principles of art and design.

name: Elements of Financial Literacy
description: This business course is designed to assist students in developing a strong foundation for making lifelong financial decisions. Making good financial choices requires integrating different kinds of information, of which financial data is only one part. Credit value is assumed to match Financial Literacy (2.5).
